newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHARES INCH UP, SEEN DOWN ON THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHARES INCH UP, SEEN DOWN ON THURSDAY.

text.p: Polish shares inched up after Tuesday's dip but analysts saw another profit-taking fall on Thursday, saying the bourse's previous foreign-fuelled surge might be reaching an end.
The market had risen 14.5 percent over six sessions.

"Maybe it was a strong wave of demand that will fade and then the market will be more stable, which can still mean growth but not at the previous pace," said Artur Kobos, a trader at ING Barings in Warsaw.
Analysts saw a fall on Thursday, the last session this week before the Assumption Day holiday on Friday.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.3 percent to 17,220.5 points and turnover inched up 1.8 percent to 278.1 million zlotys on both markets.

Analysts said that some of the large-cap firms, including banks, which led the previous uptrend could hit corrections on Thursday, such as Wednesday's top gainer PBR, up 6.3 percent with strong selling after price fixing.
Banks Gdanski and BRE were also among Wednesday's top gainers, up five and 4.1 percent respectively, the latter in heavy trade.
Analysts said a good sign was a government analyst's Wednesday comment 1997 GDP may grow 5.7 percent and inflation stay at the forecast 13 percent despite recent floods.

They said Tuesday's news the co-ruling Peasant Party (PSL) would seek to dismiss the prime minister over farm policy could be seen as electioneering ahead of September's parliamentary elections and have no significant effect on shares.
Analysts said ZEW, which fell 10 percent for the second day running and dropped 23.2 percent since resuming trade on Monday after a month-long flood suspension, should extend its fall on Thursday.
